author: M. Okafor
lede: Rev C is ready for your sign off. About ten minutes: read the summary, walk the five changes, answer four questions, then send your response to M. Okafor.
summary: Sets the checks every battery cell passes when it arrives, before it goes into an electric bike pack.
A tighter batch check, a voltage test on every cell, a new residue check, and simpler records.
More cells checked per batch, and a batch stops the moment one bad cell is found.
Whole batches can come back, so suppliers need to fix causes, not single cells.
A short session on the voltage test, the wipe test, and the new batch record.
steps: Walk the five changes. Tap any page to see it full size.
Answer the four questions and pick your decision.
Copy your response or save it as a PDF, and send it to M. Okafor in Slack, Teams, or email.

stops.title: What This Covers
text: This procedure applies to every battery cell and every cell separator film received at Lumen Cell, from all approved suppliers and their sub-tier suppliers.
No cell or film batch may be moved to stock until it passes the checks in this procedure.
around: This procedure explains how incoming battery cells are checked before they are used to build electric bike battery packs.
look: Separator film suppliers are now included, not only cell makers.
Sub-tier suppliers are covered, so a supplier's own vendors are in scope.
stops.bottom: Everything that goes inside a cell now passes the same gate.

stops.title: How Many Cells We Check
text: Pull a set number of cells from every batch: all cells for batches of 20 or fewer, 20 cells for batches of 21 to 100, and 32 cells for larger batches.
If even one sampled cell fails any check, the whole batch is rejected and set aside for review.
around: 6.1 Record the supplier, batch number, and quantity received before opening any packaging.
look: The sample size is fixed by batch size, so every inspector pulls the same number.
One bad cell rejects the whole batch. The old table allowed a few bad cells per batch.
stops.bottom: The old rule let the two problem batches through. This one would have stopped both.

stops.title: Voltage Check
text: Test the resting voltage of every sampled cell within 24 hours of arrival.
Reject any cell that reads below 3.60 volts or above 3.70 volts, and record each reading in the batch record.
around: Use the calibrated meter at the receiving bench. Let cells rest at room temperature for at least one hour before testing.
look: Is a 24 hour window workable at the receiving bench?
Do the 3.60 to 3.70 volt limits match the cell maker's sheet?
stops.bottom: Voltage is the fastest early sign of a damaged or mislabeled cell.

stops.title: Residue Check
text: Look over each sampled cell for leaked liquid, staining, or swelling, then wipe the terminals with a clean dry swab.
Any wet or discolored swab rejects the batch.
around: Wear nitrile gloves and eye protection. Dispose of used swabs in the marked bin.
look: This is a new step. Nothing like it existed in Rev B.
The wipe test needs only a swab and takes under a minute per cell.
stops.bottom: Leaked liquid was the root cause of both returns. Now it is caught at the door.

stops.title: Keeping Records
text: Record every check in the batch record and keep it for 10 years.
The paper receiving log is retired. Results live only in the batch record.
around: 7.2 Rejected batches are tagged red and moved to the hold area until reviewed.
look: Is 10 years the right length of time?
Does the batch record capture everything the paper log did?
stops.bottom: One record per batch, one place to look.

questions.q: Is the new batch check and rejection rule right?
questions.why: It is stricter, and suppliers will feel it.

questions.q: Can every sampled cell be checked against these voltage limits?
questions.why: The bench needs the meter and time to do it.

questions.q: Is the residue check clear and workable?
questions.why: It is new, so inspectors will follow the words exactly.

questions.q: Are the record changes ready to use?
questions.why: The batch record must hold the facts once the paper log ends.
